body: Order: (1) Item 8 auditor's report first - opinion type, going-concern paragraph, Critical Audit Matters (CAMs, required since 2019-20: tell you where the auditor saw the most judgment), auditor name/tenure. (2) Item 9A controls (effective or not) and Item 9 (auditor disagreements). (3) Financial statements: cash-flow statement before income statement - CFO vs net income, capex, SBC add-back, acquisitions, buybacks. (4) Notes that matter most: revenue recognition and disaggregation (segments, geography, top customers >10%), segment note, debt (maturities, covenants, rates), leases, contingencies/litigation, SBC note (dilution, unvested awards), income taxes (cash taxes vs book), goodwill/impairment tests, related parties, subsequent events. (5) Item 7 MD&A - management's own KPIs, liquidity, critical accounting estimates; compare wording year-over-year (diffing is easy with sec_fetch.py doc --text). (6) Item 1 Business (customers, competition, backlog, employees) and Item 1A Risk Factors - read only what is NEW vs last year. (7) Item 5 buybacks and Item 7A market risk. (8) Part III (Items 10-14) lives in the DEF 14A proxy: exec pay metrics (what management is paid to maximize), beneficial ownership table (Item 12, insider skin), related-party transactions (Item 13), audit vs non-audit fees (Item 14). Then 10-Qs for the latest quarters and 8-K EX-99.1 releases. Skip boilerplate risk factors and forward-looking statement pages.
title: How to read a US 10-K in 60-90 minutes: order of attack
